pages.title: File:A rubberized squid- yes, that was a live squid once! (20564597380).jpg

ObjectName.value: A rubberized squid- yes, that was a live squid once! (20564597380)

Categories.value: Plastination|Canadian Museum of Nature|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Photographs by shankar s.|June 2015 in Ottawa

ImageDescription.value: From rubber dinosaur models to rubberized real creatures. Yes, that was once a live squid swimming in the seas near you. After death, silicone was injected into the creature's body to rubberize it and to preserve all it's natural muscles and fibres. This concept was tried with human bodies initially, where an exhibition in China caused much uproar in 1995. People soon got over it, and rubberized real human exhibits are quite common nowadays. Mercifully we didn't see any rubberized human bodies, barring a human heart and a brain (we were encouraged to hold the heart in our hand!), but in this section we saw several siliconized animals. More notes in subsequent captions. (Ottawa, Canada, June 2015)
